title: Event loop blocking call
prompt_markdown: What happens if you execute `time.sleep(5)` inside an `async def` function running in asyncio?
hints: Think about single-threaded event loop behavior.

choices: Only that specific coroutine pauses; other coroutines continue running.
The entire event loop and thread block for 5 seconds, starving all coroutines.
Asyncio automatically converts it to asyncio.sleep(5).
content.explanation: time.sleep is synchronous and blocking. Because asyncio uses a single-threaded cooperative event loop, blocking the thread halts execution of all concurrent tasks.

title: Concurrent execution with gather
prompt_markdown: Which function is typically used to run multiple coroutines concurrently and collect their results?
hints: Look for the function that gathers results.

content.explanation: asyncio.gather(*aws) runs awaitable objects concurrently and returns a future aggregating results from the given coroutines.

title: Async vs Multithreading
prompt_markdown: In what scenarios does `asyncio` outperform standard OS threads, and when is it ineffective?
hints: Distinguish between I/O-bound with high concurrency and CPU-bound computation.

rubric: Explains that asyncio is ideal for high-concurrency I/O-bound tasks (network sockets, web servers) with minimal memory overhead.
Explains that asyncio cannot speed up CPU-bound tasks because of the Python GIL and single-threaded cooperative loop.
content.reference_answer: Asyncio excels at high-concurrency I/O-bound workloads (such as thousands of idle or fast web connections) because cooperative coroutines have very low memory and context-switching overhead compared to OS threads. However, it is ineffective for CPU-bound tasks (e.g. video processing or heavy math), where a long-running calculation will block the entire event loop unless offloaded to a ProcessPoolExecutor.

title: Timeout and cancellation pattern
prompt_markdown: How should an API client guard an asynchronous external request against hanging indefinitely, and what exception is handled?

rubric: Mentions using asyncio.wait_for(coroutine, timeout=...) or asyncio.timeout context manager.
content.reference_answer: Use `asyncio.wait_for(coro, timeout=seconds)` or the Python 3.11+ `async with asyncio.timeout(seconds):` context manager. If the operation exceeds the deadline, a `TimeoutError` is raised and the underlying task is cancelled.
